PLAN "3-Week Reconditioning Block: Return to Baseline"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary strength:
    name "Return to baseline after illness"

PHASES
  PHASE "Phase 1" (3 weeks):
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Monday training 60m "Reconditioning - Lower volume"
        warmup:
          walking 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          squat 3x5 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
          leg_press 3x8 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
          bench_press 3x5 rpe 6.5 rest 90 seconds
          dumbbell_row 3x8 rpe 6.5 rest 90 seconds
          overhead_press 3x6 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
        cooldown:
          shoulder_stretch 5 minutes
      DAY Wednesday training 45m "Mobility + light carryover"
        warmup:
          jog_in_place 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          hip_thrust 3x8 rpe 6.5 rest 90 seconds
          goblet_squat 3x8 rpe 6.5 rest 90 seconds
          lat_pulldown 3x8 rpe 6.5 rest 90 seconds
          face_pull 3x12 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          chest_stretch 5 minutes
      DAY Friday training 60m "Technique & light volumes"
        warmup:
          cycling 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          incline_press 3x6 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
          barbell_row 3x6 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
          rear_delt_fly 3x12 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
          tricep_pushdown 3x10 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          lying_leg_raise 5 minutes
    WEEK 2:
      DAY Monday training 60m "Progressive reintroduction"
        warmup:
          walking 6 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          squat 3x5 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
          leg_curl 3x8 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
          bench_press 3x5 rpe 6.5 rest 90 seconds
          dumbbell_row 3x8 rpe 6.5 rest 90 seconds
          overhead_press 3x6 rpe 6.5 rest 90 seconds
        cooldown:
          hip_stretch 5 minutes
      DAY Wednesday training 45m "Mobility + scapular work"
        warmup:
          jog_in_place 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          hip_thrust 3x8 rpe 6.5 rest 90 seconds
          goblet_squat 3x8 rpe 6.5 rest 90 seconds
          lat_pulldown 3x8 rpe 6.5 rest 90 seconds
          face_pull 3x12 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          shoulder_stretch 5 minutes
      DAY Friday training 60m "Technique & stabilization"
        warmup:
          cycling 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          incline_press 3x6 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
          barbell_row 3x6 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
          rear_delt_fly 3x12 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
          tricep_pushdown 3x10 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          thoracic mobility 5 minutes
    WEEK 3:
      DAY Monday training 60m "Return readiness"
        warmup:
          walking 6 minutes

          squat 3x5 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
          leg_press 3x8 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds

          dumbbell_row 3x8 rpe 6.5 rest 90 seconds
          overhead_press 3x6 rpe 6.5 rest 90 seconds

          quad_stretch 5 minutes
      DAY Wednesday training 45m "Light technique"
        warmup:
          jog_in_place 5 minutes

          goblet_squat 3x8 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
          lat_pulldown 3x8 rpe 6.5 rest 90 seconds
          incline_press 3x6 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
          dumbbell_row 3x8 rpe 6.5 rest 90 seconds
        cooldown:
          back_stretch 5 minutes
      DAY Friday training 60m "Lower intensity deload"

          cycling 5 minutes

PLAN "Nutrition targets for 3-week reconditioning block"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary nutrition:
    name "Calorie and protein targets to support reconditioning and return to baseline"

PHASES
  PHASE "Phase 1" (3 weeks):
    WEEK 1:
      DAY N/A "Daily nutrition targets":
        main/macronutrients:
          calories 2600..2800
          protein 170..200 grams
          carbohydrates 320..360 grams
          fats 70..90 grams
        notes:
          - aim for protein floor 1.6 g/kg, adjust to maintain weight
          - include protein with every meal and post-workout
          - hydrate 2.5–3 liters daily
          - monitor weight 0.5 kg weekly; adjust calories by ±250 if weight trend not ~0.5 kg/week
    WEEK 2:
      DAY N/A "Daily nutrition targets (tuned)":
        main/macronutrients:
          calories 2700..2900
          protein 170..210 grams
          carbohydrates 320..380 grams
          fats 75..95 grams
        notes:
          - increase carbs on training days; lower slightly on rest/tech days
          - prioritize recovery meals post-session
    WEEK 3:
      DAY N/A "Daily nutrition targets (maintenance readiness)":
        main/macronutrients:
          calories 2800..3000
          protein 170..210 grams
          carbohydrates 340..400 grams
          fats 75..95 grams
        notes:
          - aim to steady weight near baseline
          - ensure sufficient sleep and overall energy availability

Reasoning on skipping Week 1 and starting at pre-illness loads

- Context:
  - 3 weeks off due to mild flu with persistent fatigue and 4 kg weight loss.
  - Pre-illness loads: bench 100 kg, squat 140 kg, deadlift 170 kg.
  - Yesterday plan: Week 1 loads (lower volume, reconditioning) with targeted RPEs and lighter volumes to re-establish technique and tolerance.

- Considerations for skipping Week 1:
  - Fatigue and infection history: Even mild illness can dampen central drive, hormonal signaling, and recovery capacity. Returning to peak pre-illness loads immediately risks overreaching, immune re-suppression, or injury if tolerance is not yet restored.
  - 4 kg weight loss: This often signals energy deficit or recent illness impact. Jumping back to top-end loads without a gradual reintroduction can impair performance and recovery and may prolong the reconditioning timeline.
  - Training age and current status: An intermediate lifter with a 3-week layoff often benefits from a stepped approach: reintroduce movement patterns, gradually increase volume, and re-establish RPE baselines before loading near max or prior PRs.

- Risks of starting at pre-illness loads now:
  - Acute fatigue underestimation: Even with normal energy today, glycogen stores, sleep quality, and systemic recovery may not be back to baseline.
  - Technique risk: Moving heavy loads with compromised form after a layoff increases knee/ back/ shoulder risk.
  - Illness rebound: If latent symptoms or delayed onset fatigue appear, there’s a higher chance of pushing into stalled progress.

- Benefits of a cautious start (Week 1 style) vs immediate heavy loads:
  - Assess tolerance: Week 1 acts as a diagnostic to gauge current strength and recovery capacity at manageable intensities.
  - Consolidate technique: Lower volume/volume-deload while reactivating nervous system and connective tissue readiness.
  - Psychological: Builds confidence to handle loads again without fear of relapse into fatigue.

- Practical approach if you consider skipping Week 1:
  - Optional partial Week 1: Use Week 1 but reduce load modestly (e.g., 5–10% cut) or keep the same exercises with lighter reps or RPE, then resume Week 2 at closer to pre-illness targets.
  - Implement a “tuned” Week 1: 
    - Keep squat/bench/deadlift but drop 1–2 reps per set or reduce one set per lift.
    - Use RPE 5–6 instead of 6–6.5.
    - Maintain cardio but at lower volume/impact if needed.
  - Monitor: Track daily energy, mood, sleep, and any signs of abnormal fatigue. If any persistent symptoms, back off.

- Recommendation:
  - Do not fully skip Week 1. If the client feels fine, run Week 1 with a conservative lens:
    - Slightly reduced sets/reps or a modest load reduction (e.g., 5–10% less than pre-illness loads) to re-establish tolerance.
    - Use RPE targets around 5–6 for the first sessions, then reassess mid-week.
    - Keep cardio volume modest (e.g., 10–15 minutes) to avoid excessive energy drain.
  - If performance and recovery feel exceptionally smooth after Day 1 of Week 1, you can progressively approach Week 1 targets more quickly or proceed to Week 2 as planned.

- Suggested plan if you want a concrete pathway:
  - Week 1 (modified): 
    - Bench_press: 3x5 @ RPE 5–6, loads around 85–90% of pre-illness or maintain same weight with fewer reps if form feels off.
    - Squat: 3x5 @ RPE 5–6, similar load adjustment.
    - Deadlift: 2x5 @ RPE 5–6, lighter than pre-illness if needed.
    - Cardio: keep light 10–15 minutes, avoid high intensity near lifting days.
  - If Day 1 feels great (RPE 6 or less, good recovery), you can progress toward Week 1 targets by Day 2–3 and move into Week 2 on schedule, but remain vigilant for signs of fatigue.

- Bottom line:
  - It is reasonable to reassess after Day 1 rather than wholesale skip Week 1. Proceed with a cautious reintroduction that respects remaining recovery needs, with a plan to escalate to pre-illness loads only after 1–2 weeks of solid tolerance. Prioritize form, recovery, and nutrition to support return to baseline.

PLAN " readiness signals for full intensity work"
TYPE guidance
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary guidance:
    name "Signals to resume full intensity after illness/layoff"

PHASES
  PHASE "Phase 1" (3 weeks):
    WEEK 1:
      DAY N/A "Readiness signals checklist":
        signals:
          - sleep_quality: "7+ hours on most nights; no persistent insomnia"
          - resting_hr_trend: "no >5 bpm increase over baseline across 3 days"
          - appetite: "stable or increasing from prior week"
          - weight_change: "within ±0.5 kg from post-illness baseline"
          - energy: "daily energy 6/10 or higher, no persistent fatigue"
          - mood: "no persistent low mood or anhedonia"
          - training_tusion: "able to complete planned Week 1 with RPE ≤6 on all lifts"
          - technique_checks: "no egregious form deviations on core lifts during sets"
          - biomarker_tolerance: "if available, stable HRV within normal range"
        actions_on_go_signal:
          - proceed_to_full_intensity_work: "when all core signals at or near baseline for 3 consecutive sessions"
        actions_on_warning:
          - pause_or_downshift: "if any red flags appear (severe fatigue, chest tightness, dizziness, fever, >2 consecutive days sleep disruption, persistent high resting HR >10 bpm above baseline)"
    WEEK 2:
      DAY N/A "Progression decision rules":
        proceed_if:
          - above_signals: "most readiness signals green on 4 of 5 days"
        hold_if:
          - mixed_signals: "some drift but no red flags; continue with monitored progression"
        revert_if:
          - red_flags: "fever, chest pain, orthostatic intolerance, inability to complete sessions"
    WEEK 3:
      DAY N/A "Final decision window":
        ready_for_full_intensity: "≥2 consecutive sessions at target full loads with RPE 7–9 and no adverse symptoms"
        back-off_needed: "any recurrence of fatigue, mood drop, sleep disruption, or weight loss >1 kg"

NOTES
  - Use objective markers where possible (sleep, resting HR, weight, appetite, mood, training tolerance).
  - If unavailable telemetry, rely on subjective tolerance and ability to complete sessions with requested RPE targets and correct technique.
  - Prioritize gradual reintroduction rather than abrupt load jumps; otherwise risk prolonged recovery.

OUTPUT_EXAMPLE
  - Signals checklist template to place into athlete journal or tracking app.
  - If ready, escalate to full-intensity phase per plan.

PLAN "Week 3 Target Loads + 1RM Test Integration"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary strength:
    name "Week 3 integration of 1RM test to reset programming"

PHASES
  PHASE "Phase 1" (3 weeks):
    WEEK 3:
      DAY Monday training 60m "Final readiness + 1RM testing window":
        warmup:
          walking 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          squat 2x3 rpe 6 rest 180 seconds
          bench_press 2x3 rpe 6 rest 180 seconds
          deadlift 2x3 rpe 6 rest 180 seconds
        1RM_test:
          squat_1rm:
            attempts 2
            rest_between_attempts 15 minutes
            targets:
              - attempt_1: "target around 90% of pre-illness estimate, e.g., 120–130 kg as a light opener"
              - attempt_2: "open to PR attempt if technique solid and RPE tolerable, otherwise stop"
          bench_press_1rm:
            attempts 2
            rest_between_attempts 15 minutes
            targets:
              - attempt_1: "target around 90% of pre-illness, e.g., 90–95 kg"
              - attempt_2: "PR attempt if confident and solid form"
          deadlift_1rm:
            attempts 2
            rest_between_attempts 15 minutes
            targets:
              - attempt_1: "target around 85–95% of pre-illness, e.g., 140–150 kg"
              - attempt_2: "PR attempt if setup and form are clean"
        cooldown:
          full_body_light_stretch 5 minutes
      DAY Wednesday training 45m "1RM results review + programming reset":
        warmup:
          jog_in_place 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          squat 3x5 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
          bench_press 3x5 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
          deadlift 2x5 rpe 6 rest 120 seconds
        cooldown:
          thoracic_mobility 5 minutes
      DAY Friday training 60m "Post-1RM deload + plan reset":
        warmup:
          cycling 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          squat 3x5 rpe 5 rest 90 seconds
          bench_press 3x5 rpe 5 rest 90 seconds
          deadlift 2x5 rpe 5 rest 120 seconds
        cooldown:
          hip_stretch 5 minutes

NOTE
  - 1RM attempts should be only after adequate warmup and if readiness signals are positive to minimize injury risk.
  - If 1RM attempts show suboptimal tolerance, revert to progressive overload plan with submax loads and reassess in subsequent sessions.
  - Use 1RM results to anchor Phase 2 programming targets (new working weights and progression scheme).
